Overview

Gaborone as a Business Centre

Gaborone is Botswana's capital and principal business centre, in the south-east of the country about 15 kilometres from the South African border. Statistics Botswana's 2022 census counted about 246,000 residents in the city. Government ministries, the National Assembly and most regulators are based here, and the city hosts the headquarters of the Southern African Development Community. Botswana's economy depends heavily on diamonds: Debswana, a 50:50 venture between the government and De Beers, generates about half of government revenue, and diamond sorting, cutting and polishing businesses have developed in Gaborone. The Botswana Stock Exchange, established in 1989, lists just under 40 companies, including major banks and retailers.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Gaborone because it is where Botswana's government contracts, diamond sales relationships and financial sector licences are decided. Suppliers to mining, infrastructure and public procurement often need to understand the ownership and political connections of local partners, and investors need reliable information about companies whose legal owners appear in the CIPA register but whose beneficial owners may not be visible. Weaker diamond demand since the early 2020s, linked partly to lab-grown stones, has added financial stress for some counterparties. With more than 5,000 commercial matters reported pending before the High Court in 2026, counsel also need well-sourced facts to support litigation and enforcement.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Gaborone

01

Diamond sector counterparty diligence

Background research on diamond traders, cutting and polishing businesses, sightholders and service providers operating in Gaborone, covering ownership, management, financial position, litigation and reputation, at a time when weaker demand for mined diamonds is putting pressure on parts of the value chain.

02

Public tender and procurement disputes

Factual support for counsel in disputes over government and parastatal tenders awarded from Gaborone, including research into bidders' ownership, directors, related companies, prior contract performance and any public connections to officials, using lawful public sources and court records.

03

CIPA ownership and partner research

Mapping the shareholders, directors and connected entities of Botswana companies through the CIPA online register and related filings, and testing whether a proposed local partner, agent or joint venture party is who it claims to be before contracts are signed.

04

Financial services and listed company research

Research on banks, insurers, asset managers, microlenders and companies listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange, including regulatory status, published disclosures, key individuals and litigation, for investors, lenders, insurers and acquirers that are considering Gaborone-based financial businesses.

05

Asset research in commercial and divorce disputes

Supporting counsel in commercial claims and in complex divorces involving business interests before the Gaborone High Court, through lawful research into companies, directorships, property and assets connected to a party, organised so that counsel can assess enforcement options.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Gaborone

High Court and new Commercial Court

The High Court has a division in Gaborone, which with the Lobatse division carried a backlog reported in 2026 at more than 5,000 commercial matters and more than 2,000 divorce cases. In spring 2026 the Judiciary launched Botswana's first specialised Commercial Court, operating initially in the Gaborone and Lobatse divisions. It is reported to hear commercial litigation, public tender disputes, corruption and economic crime matters, and complex divorces involving business assets, as part of the Administration of Justice reform agenda.

Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime

The Directorate on Corruption and Economic Crime (DCEC), established in 1994 under the Corruption and Economic Crime Act, is headquartered in Gaborone. It investigates corruption and economic crime and relies heavily on whistleblower reports. Its public cases and court outcomes are a useful source when assessing counterparties connected to government contracts, though TDSC uses only published information and does not seek access to DCEC investigations.

CIPA and company records

The Companies and Intellectual Property Authority, based in Gaborone, maintains the company and business names register through its online system, launched in 2019. Legal ownership and director information can generally be searched online, and companies are required to disclose beneficial owners, though public access to that data has varied. Court files and land records usually require local retrieval, which TDSC arranges through appropriately qualified local professionals when justified.

Financial regulators and exchange

Gaborone is home to the Bank of Botswana, which supervises banks, the Non-Bank Financial Institutions Regulatory Authority (NBFIRA), which oversees insurers, pension funds, asset managers and other non-bank financial services, and the Botswana Stock Exchange. Licensing lists, regulatory notices and listed company disclosures provide verifiable information about financial counterparties, including audited accounts, directors and major shareholders of listed issuers. Such disclosures are dated and checkable.

Regional and international presence

As the seat of the SADC secretariat and of regional development programmes, Gaborone attracts consultants, contractors and organisations working across southern Africa. Matters touching the city can therefore involve counterparties incorporated in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia or elsewhere in the region, and research often needs to combine Botswana records with company and court information from neighbouring jurisdictions. Cross-border links should be checked early.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Gaborone

For matters touching Gaborone, TDSC starts by defining the commercial question: who controls a tender winner, whether a diamond sector counterparty is financially stable, or which assets a party in a High Court dispute holds. Research is conducted from Nashville using the CIPA register, Botswana Stock Exchange and regulator publications, published judgments, DCEC announcements and local and regional press, combined with records in South Africa and other neighbouring jurisdictions where structures connect. Where court file retrieval, land searches or interviews are needed, TDSC coordinates with appropriately qualified Botswana professionals and the client's counsel. Personal data is handled under Botswana's data protection law with a defined purpose and minimised collection.

TDSC has no office in Gaborone. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Gaborone: Frequently Asked Questions

What is Botswana's new Commercial Court and does it sit in Gaborone?

The Judiciary launched Botswana's first specialised Commercial Court in spring 2026, initially operating in the Gaborone and Lobatse divisions of the High Court. Reports describe it as handling commercial litigation, tender disputes, corruption and economic crime, and complex divorces involving business interests. Counsel should confirm its current rules and thresholds, since detailed procedures were still being reported when this page was prepared.

Can you find out who really owns a Gaborone company?

The CIPA online register usually shows directors and legal shareholders, and companies are required to disclose beneficial owners, but public access to that information has been inconsistent. We combine register data with filings, court records, press and regional company records to build a picture of control, and we state clearly what is documented and what is inferred.

Can you research a counterparty in the diamond trade?

Yes. We research ownership, management, related companies, litigation, regulatory and press history of diamond traders, manufacturers and service providers connected to Gaborone. We rely on lawful public and commercial sources and do not seek confidential sales or allocation information from Debswana, De Beers or government bodies.

Can you help in a dispute over a government tender?

We support counsel by researching the bidders, their shareholders and directors, related companies, prior contract performance and any publicly reported links to officials. The legal challenge itself, including procurement rules and remedies, remains with Botswana counsel. Our role is to provide accurate, sourced facts that help them assess and present the case.

Does TDSC have an office in Gaborone?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Gaborone or elsewhere in Botswana. Most work is desk-based research. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately qualified Botswana professionals and the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving pretexting, covert recording or access to restricted government records.
